mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-23.7 to -20.3), indicating positive momentum in retail footfall recovery that is likely to persist absent a reversal shock, pushing the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC 4-week-ahead mean falls below the trailing 4-week mean despite three or more consecutive weeks of prior increase.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 5 points over a rolling 3-week window, it signals renewed commuting and errand-running capacity that mechanically feeds retail and recreation footfall within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points from t-3w to t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -30.9 to -24.7 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks even though TRANSIT improved by more than 5 points over the prior 3 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sustained improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a compounding return to normal daily circulation patterns; their joint rise amplifies retail footfall more than either series alone, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved each week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than when only one of WORKPLACES or TRANSIT rises, indicating no amplification effect.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent week-over-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (14.0 to 11.7) reflects households spending less time confined at home, a behavioral shift that translates into increased discretionary outings and higher RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 14.0 to 11.7 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 2 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL continues its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility exceeding 4 points signals a newly imposed outdoor-gathering restriction; such policy tightening historically coincides with reduced general mobility, including a suppressive effect on RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -9.3 to -12.6 between t-2w and t-1w, a 3.3-point drop
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a greater-than-4-point drop in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed in a narrow band near -5 to -7 percent, consistent with stable essential-trip behavior typical of a non-holiday seasonal period; without a seasonal demand shock, discretionary retail activity captured by RETAIL_REC is unlikely to accelerate and may plateau or dip over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM oscillated between -4.3 and -7.1 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next 4 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, indicating no seasonal plateau effect.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of falling RESIDENTIAL and rising WORKPLACES indicates a coordinated behavioral shift away from home-centric routines toward out-of-home activity; this combination predicts a stronger rebound in RETAIL_REC than either series moving alone would suggest.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines and WORKPLACES rises concurrently for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell while WORKPLACES rose in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 2 weeks is not greater than predicted by WORKPLACES alone, indicating no interaction effect with RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility reverses and falls by more than 5 points within a single week after a period of recovery, it signals re-imposition of movement restrictions or a public health response, which would rapidly suppress RETAIL_REC within the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops by more than 5 points in a single week after at least two prior weeks of improvement
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved for three consecutive weeks prior to the decision point
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a sudden greater-than-5-point drop in TRANSIT after a recovery trend.
